evidence.text:
王仲祖聞蠻語不解茫然曰若使介葛盧來朝故當
不昩此語

蔡司徒渡江見彭蜞大喜曰蟹有八足加以二螯令
烹之既食吐下委頓方知非蟹後向謝仁祖說此事
謝曰卿讀爾雅不熟幾為勸學死

judgment.explanation: 劉眞長 is Liu Zhenchang (Liu Tan 劉惔), a well-known Eastern Jin figure. The candidate c0 supplies 劉眞長 as the name, matching the surface form directly. The main text lists him as one of the three visitors to Yin Yangzhou's grave. The candidate is the historical referent.

The annotation describes Hao's reclusive behavior, consistent with the main text's account of 殷揚州's refusal to serve. The candidate is the historical referent.

assertions.exact_span: 王仲祖謝仁祖劉眞長俱至丹陽墓所省殷揚州
assertions.interpretation: The three men together went to the tomb site at Danyang to visit Yin Yangzhou (Yin Hao); this is the main scene of the narrative.
assertions.surface: 俱至丹陽墓所省殷揚州

assertions.interpretation: They were deeply worried and sighed, describing their emotional state at the moment of discussion.
Over many years, repeated summons were issued but Yin Hao did not come; this is background context preceding the scene explaining his refusal to take office.
The Zhongxing shu records that Yin Hao lingered/remained in seclusion; this is background context about his state of withdrawal.

assertion.interpretation: At the time of the visit, Yin Hao displayed a firm, resolute resolve (not to rise to office), describing his state during the scene.
After returning from the tomb visit, Wang and Xie discussed the matter; this marks a subsequent moment relative to the scene.
Wang and Xie expressed deep worry that if Yuanyuan (Yin Hao) did not rise to office, what would become of the people; this is their concern voiced at the time after returning.

assertion.exact_span: 卿諸人眞憂淵源不起邪
assertion.interpretation: Liu Zhenchang's retort questioning whether they truly worried about Yuanyuan not rising; this is part of the dialogue in the scene.
